What each level looks like

  1. L1Awareness: what L1 means for any competency

    Recognise that ethics, law, and tech are moving fast in PDS and that yesterday's answer may not still hold.

  2. L2Familiarity: what L2 means for any competency

    Follow at least one credible source (newsletter, regulator update, professional body) regularly.

  3. L3Proficiency: what L3 means for any competencyTarget working level

    Maintain working knowledge across ethics, law, and tech and bring relevant updates into the team's practice.

  4. L4Mastery: what L4 means for any competency

    Lead horizon-scanning for the team and translate developments into concrete changes.

  5. L5Expertise: what L5 means for any competency

    Help shape the field externally — talks, working groups, publications.

Level names link to what that level means for any competency.

At L1, cannot yet: produce work in this area without close guidance.

Signal for moving up to L2: has completed a guided exercise (course, tutorial, paired session) end-to-end.

At L2, cannot yet: choose between methods on their own, or handle data that doesn't match the template.

Signal for moving up to L3: has independently delivered usable output on a real pharma problem they hadn't seen a template for.

At L3, cannot yet (reliably): handle problems where the standard recipes don't apply, or notice when a non-standard situation is hiding behind a standard-looking one.

Signal for moving up to L4: has handled at least one problem where the obvious approach didn't work, recognized that, and chosen a different one with a defensible reason.

At L4, cannot yet (necessarily): change what the broader team or field considers good practice.

Signal for moving up to L5: has changed how others work — through teaching, a published method, an internal standard, or an open-source contribution that others adopted.
